hero.headline: I am Matija Radeljak. This dashboard is one of the things I make in my free time.

why_this.title: Why this exists
paragraphs: The freedom of any society depends, more than on anything else, on how well informed it is.

That much is common knowledge. Croatia also has working open-data portals, national ([data.gov.hr](https://data.gov.hr)) and local ([data.zagreb.hr](https://data.zagreb.hr)). And yet almost none of the institutions that spend public money on culture in this country put anything on them, or show by any other means the slightest interest in making their past and current data easy to reach and easy to read for the public that wants it.

That missing transparency helps hold a culturally stunted status quo in place, and out of that status quo come initiatives and decisions — scientifically, technically and morally dubious ones — in corners of public life that have nothing to do with culture: activism, investigative journalism, politics, purely commercial industry, civil society, and, of course, culture and the arts themselves. Put plainly: when the record and the facts are out of reach, that alone decides which people and which companies get to act on their creative, professional and even personal ideas, and which do not. Which sits in flat contradiction to the free, meritocratic society everybody claims to believe in and most take for granted.

I built this in my own free time, out of that conviction and out of having the technical means to do something about it — and, before anything else, as a demonstration of what is technically possible, measured the plainest way there is: hours in, result out.

Turning the published PDFs into structured datasets and building the application on top of them took about 60 working hours, spread over 6 weeks and 3 “eras” of different approaches, creative development, coding, testing, repairs and revisions (see the [Process](#/process) tab). Most of it was done between 10 and 31 May 2026.

The application runs on a free Cloudflare Worker and weighs 22.6 MiB in total, of which 22.2 MiB is the database itself ([data.json](https://havc.matijar.info/havc/data.json)). The code is plain HTML, JavaScript and CSS, which means there are no third-party dependencies. FontAwesome icons and Google Fonts are used for presentation; nothing stops working without them.
The code, and the whole history of how it was built, revised and checked, is public: [github.com/matijarma/havc-explorer](https://github.com/matijarma/havc-explorer).

who_i_am.title: Who I am
paragraphs: I have been studying art and computing, actively and with something to say about both, from about as early as a person can. It started before primary school did, and not long after primary school came the drama studio of the Zagreb Youth Theatre, where I grew up and spent my formative years. A lifelong love of drama and screen acting turned into something else once I came of age and failed the acting entrance exam at Zagreb's Academy of Dramatic Art: first into film directing, then into creative producing — a description I fit so well that I am not often shy about saying I am the only authentic creative producer in Croatia. Given that the creative producer is not, as a rule, one of the more flattering archetypes in European film culture, the joke is less rude than it first sounds.

While all that growing up was happening on stage and in the shabby auditoriums of Zagreb's cinemas, I was also, from the same early age, following every hertz and every byte of every electronic device I was allowed to touch. Devouring books, films and plays with one hand and taking apart every piece of software and hardware within reach with the other, I settled on drama and computing as the two fields I would work in and draw from. That childhood happened to coincide with The Matrix, Pretty Village Pretty Flame, Titanic, Pulp Fiction, What Iva Recorded and Fight Club; with the birth of the internet and everything that came out of it; and with a post-war Croatia corrupt at every level, which it has not stopped being since. So I don't think it is especially improbable that I came out of it a film producer who treats computing not merely as a domain and a tool, but as a safe harbour — a way to standardise, a way to be transparent, and a guarantee of the efficient systems that the fragile budgets of independent art depend on. Independent art whose authors and audiences are, almost without exception, at the mercy of middlemen and self-appointed third parties whose interests outrank the work itself, or even the audience's simple wish to see it.
This application is the simplest possible demonstration of that: raw data and statistics at once, all of it from what has been sitting on HAVC's own official website the whole time.

In September 2026 I will submit this as a project to HAVC's call for funding complementary activities. Most of the budget goes to a single line: the hours needed to obtain the data from HAVC and to clean and check it by hand, so the final datasets can be published with a guarantee that they are one hundred per cent correct.
